title: Without Coveting
note: He defines this as not thinking of seizing what belongs to others. It follows the chapter on envy, to say that beyond resenting what others have, even the thought of taking it is a fault.

couplets.plain: If you lose your fairness and covet good wealth, it destroys your family and brings you faults then and there.
couplets.pm: Fairness is knowing that taking what belongs to others isn’t righteous. Covet their good wealth without it, and the coveting ruins your family and at once brings you many faults. It is called good wealth because by nature it makes a family grow and does much good.

links.reason: Coveting good wealth without fairness brings down your family and brings faults at once.

couplets.plain: Those ashamed of unfairness won’t covet a gain and do what brings blame.
couplets.pm: Those who fear to be unfair won’t want the gain that comes from seizing others’ wealth, and won’t do the blameworthy things that seizing takes. Fairness here is knowing that no one has a claim on another’s wealth.

links.quote: won’t covet a gain and do what brings blame
links.reason: Refusing to covet goes hand in hand with refusing deeds that bring blame.

couplets.plain: Those who want that other joy won’t covet a small pleasure and do what is unrighteous.
couplets.pm: Those who long for the lasting joy that comes from righteousness won’t want the passing pleasure of stolen wealth, or do unrighteous things to the people they would take it from. It comes by sin and dies at once, which is why it is called small.

links.reason: Those with another joy in view do not covet small pleasures or do wrong to get them.

couplets.plain: People who have conquered their senses and see without flaw don’t say “We have nothing” and covet.
couplets.pm: Those who have conquered the five senses and have flawless understanding won’t think “we are poor” and want others’ wealth to end it. Conquering means not letting the senses go down the path of sin. Such people have no poverty, so they have no coveting. Flawless understanding is knowing things without distortion.

links.quote: don’t say “We have nothing” and covet

couplets.plain: What use is a fine, wide understanding if you covet and do senseless things to anyone at all?
couplets.pm: What good is an understanding that is subtle and has gone through all the books, if the wise want wealth and do senseless things to anyone? That means low and harsh acts towards worthy and unworthy alike. The use of understanding is in not doing them.

links.quote: What use is a fine, wide understanding if you covet
links.reason: Coveting empties out the worth of even the subtlest mind.

couplets.plain: Someone who seeks compassion and stands on the path will perish if they covet wealth and plot evil.
couplets.pm: Someone who wants the righteousness of compassion and stands in household life, the path to it, is ruined by merely thinking of wrongful ways to get others’ wealth. Only household life ripens the understanding needed to renounce. Ruin is losing both kinds of righteousness. If thinking ruins, doing needs no saying.

links.quote: perish if they covet wealth and plot evil

couplets.plain: Don’t want the gain that coveting brings. When it ripens, the fruit is hardly ever good.
couplets.pm: Give up wanting the gain that comes from coveting others’ wealth, because when you come to enjoy it later, its fruit won’t turn out well.

links.quote: When it ripens, the fruit is hardly ever good
links.reason: Warns that the gain from coveting will bear no good fruit when it ripens.

couplets.plain: What keeps your wealth from shrinking? Not coveting the wealth in another’s hands.
couplets.pm: Wealth by nature shrinks. If you ask what keeps it from shrinking, it is not wanting for yourself the wealth another person holds and wants. The wealth of someone who doesn’t covet won’t shrink.

links.quote: Not coveting the wealth in another’s hands
links.reason: Offers a plain bargain: leave another’s wealth alone and your own will hold.

couplets.plain: Fortune knows the way, and comes to the wise who know righteousness and don’t covet.
couplets.pm: When the wise know that this is righteousness and don’t want others’ wealth, the goddess of fortune knows the means of reaching them and comes by it. The means are the right time, place and occasion.

links.reason: Knowing righteousness and not coveting is what draws fortune to you.
Fortune is pictured as knowing the way and coming to the wise.

couplets.plain: Coveting without thought breeds destruction. The pride of wanting nothing breeds victory.
couplets.pm: Thinking of taking another’s wealth without knowing what follows brings your end, because it swells both enmity and sin. The wealth of not wanting it brings victory, because it puts below you all who go about wanting it.
couplets.note: செருக்கு is pride. He takes it as wealth, the thing that gives pride.

links.reason: Coveting that never looks ahead gives birth to destruction.

links.quote: The pride of wanting nothing breeds victory
links.reason: The pride of wanting nothing is said to breed victory.

ideaLinks.quote: Coveting without thought breeds destruction. The pride of wanting nothing breeds victory
ideaLinks.reason: Coveting breeds destruction while the pride of wanting nothing breeds victory.
